clue.text: Rich man not completely welcome in Wales and America

indicators.note: the Welsh greeting is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: croeso is the Welsh word for welcome
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A wealthy man is given only a half-hearted reception in Wales and the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' drops the last O of CROESO, the Welsh for welcome, leaving CROES.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus, the ancient king of Lydia, is proverbial for great wealth, so he is the archetypal rich man.

clue.text: 11 of 9 shot, first of all

parts.note: a shot is a photograph, informally a pic

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word all is taken

explanation.surface: A measurement unit is fired off before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is UNIT and 9 is MEASUREMENT, so '11 of 9' means a unit of measurement throughout this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The pica is a printer's unit of type size, one sixth of an inch, so it is a unit of measurement.

clue.text: 11 of 9's sound

definitions.meaning: a unit of measurement, here one of six feet used for water depth
to sound is to measure the depth of water, or to get to the bottom of something

explanation.surface: A unit of measurement makes a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathom is a six-foot unit of depth, and to fathom water is to plumb or sound it.

clue.text: Prisoner has to invite disregard for the law

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
to invite trouble is to tempt it

explanation.surface: An inmate is tempted to flout the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt of court is a wilful disrespect for the authority of the law, hence disregard for it.

clue.text: 51 pounds gets one elderly cleaner

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
quids is slang for pounds sterling
an OAP is an old-age pensioner, one elderly person

explanation.surface: A pensioner gets paid fifty-one pounds as a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: QUID is British slang for a pound; an OAP is an old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid soap is a cleaning product, a cleaner for hands or dishes.

clue.text: Bank of Scotland pens hostile letters, reader feels

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the bank holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a brae is a Scottish word for a hillside or bank
ill as in ill will, unfriendly

explanation.surface: The Bank of Scotland writes threatening letters that the reader takes to heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank of Scotland' is not the bank but a Scottish word for a slope, BRAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Braille is a writing system of raised dots that a blind reader feels with the fingertips.

clue.text: Coming back, artist's in conflict

indicators.note: the artist's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a rival is someone competing, in conflict with another

explanation.surface: Returning home, a painter finds himself in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is the act of coming somewhere, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: This may appear in lines on fancy patio?

definitions.text: This may appear in lines on fancy patio?

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine, so the letters are freely reshaped

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A garden feature that might stand in rows on an ornate patio.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipped shrubs shaped into ornamental forms are often set out in rows around a patio.

clue.text: Size of solid pieces, in essence

indicators.note: the solid pieces are placed within the essence

parts.note: the meat of something is its essence or core
sure as in solid, dependable
men are pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: The size of chunks of solid matter, essentially.
explanation.definitionFit: A measurement gives the dimensions of a thing, and size is one such dimension.

clue.text: 11 in reserve

definitions.meaning: a military unit, here a body of troops sent off on a task

explanation.surface: A unit held back in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment is a squad of troops, a unit, and also a cool aloofness or reserve of manner.

clue.text: One can start to use wheels

indicators.note: to wheel round is to turn about, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: the first letter of the word use is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is able to begin using a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is a tin; 'wheels' turns TIN plus U around.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, one whole counted on its own.

clue.text: Use a rickety crossing by a river, monsieur — prepare to fight for France

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters straddle the middle pieces, going across them
something rickety is shaky and unsound, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: by as in multiplication, three by four, written as the times sign

explanation.surface: Use an unsteady bridge over a river, monsieur, and get ready to fight for France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' stands for the times sign, as in three by four. 'rickety' makes AUSEA-style jumble AUES, which goes 'crossing' the middle letters, split either side.
explanation.definitionFit: The French call 'To arms!' from the Marseillaise, urging citizens to take up weapons for France.

clue.text: Like a diet of worms? That's a cooking ingredient

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: to worm is to wriggle, so these letters wriggle into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about the Diet of Worms, the 1521 assembly at which Luther was tried, turned into a kitchen item.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diet of Worms was the imperial assembly in the German city of Worms; here 'worms' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Asafoetida is a pungent resin used as a spice in Indian cookery, so it is an ingredient.

clue.text: 11 spy sheltering from the French

indicators.note: the spy covers and protects the French word inside it

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
du is French for of the or from the

explanation.surface: A unit's secret agent hides away from the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A module is a self-contained component or section, a unit of a larger whole.

clue.text: 9 politician to wear raincoat when going out

indicators.note: a garment worn surrounds its wearer, so the coat letters go around the politician
going out suggests being thrown off course, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A politician puts on a mackintosh before going outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' looks like leaving the house but signals the anagram, CARATION; 'to wear' puts the politician inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibration is the act of checking an instrument's readings against a standard, a form of measuring.

clue.text: Extremely close penetrating cut close to the bone

indicators.note: the end letters pierce and go into the cut

parts.note: an indent is a notch or cut

indicators.note: taking the extremes, the first and last letters of close

explanation.surface: A very near cut that goes right through.
explanation.walkthrough: The word close appears twice: the first is the source of the extremes for 'Extremely', and 'penetrating' sets them into the cut; the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Humour that is close to the bone is risqué, verging on improper or offensive.

clue.text: 11 of 9 live long at first after 01/12

indicators.note: the life and length pieces follow the date piece

parts.note: in British dating 01/12 is the first of December, DEC I
to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word long is taken

explanation.surface: Measure units live long after the first of December.
explanation.walkthrough: British dates put the day first, so 01/12 is 1 December: DEC plus I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The decibel is the unit used to measure sound intensity, a unit of measurement.

clue.text: Awful strain placed on a Russian lady

indicators.note: in a down clue the single letter sits on, so below, the reshuffled word
awful suggests something badly made, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful burden is put on a Russian woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar or an empress of Russia, a Russian noblewoman.

clue.text: 11 of 9 post bags initially checked over

indicators.note: to bag is to capture, so the posting holds the initials within

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it

indicators.note: the first letters of checked and over are taken

explanation.surface: A unit of measurement mails sacks that were checked over first.
explanation.definitionFit: The second is the basic unit of time, so it is a unit of measurement.

clue.text: Simple to unravel 9 marker?

indicators.note: to unravel is to untangle, so the letters are pulled apart and rewoven

explanation.surface: An easy-to-decipher measurement marker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' belongs in the anagram fodder with SIMPLE, giving the eight letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A milepost is a roadside post showing distances in miles, a marker of measured length.

clue.text: Poorly promote university as record breaker

indicators.note: the pieces break into the record, splitting it apart

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
to aid a cause is to promote it

explanation.surface: Badly promoting a university as a record-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone laid up is confined to bed through illness, so out of action and poorly.

clue.text: 11 of 9 detective books

parts.note: PI is a private investigator, a detective
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A unit of measurement for private-eye novels.
explanation.definitionFit: The pint is a unit of liquid capacity, so a unit of measurement.

clue.text: 11 of 9's life in focus

indicators.note: the lifetime piece is set inside the focus piece

parts.note: the centre of attention is its focus
one's time is one's life span

explanation.surface: A unit of measurement's existence comes into sharp view.
explanation.definitionFit: The centimetre is a hundredth of a metre, a metric unit of length.

clue.text: What kipper will do mostly over fish

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so read upwards
most of the word is used, its final letter lost

parts.note: a kipper is a nap or someone sleeping, so a kipper will sleep

explanation.surface: A smoked herring sits mostly atop some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kipper' is not the fish but a sleeper; 'mostly' trims SLEEP to SLEE and 'over' turns it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish, so the plural noun matches the plural sense here.

clue.text: 9 Royals in Berkshire

definitions.meaning: a figure taken from a meter or gauge, a measurement
the football club nicknamed the Royals is based in a Berkshire town

explanation.surface: A measure of the royal family in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is an English county west of London; its football club Reading FC is nicknamed the Royals.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge reading is a value taken from an instrument, and the Berkshire town shares the name.

clue.text: 11 of 9's hair in need of a cut?

parts.note: fur is an animal's hair
hair that wants a trim is long

explanation.surface: A unit of measurement's mane is overdue for a trim.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's question mark hints that the phrase reads as fur that is long.
explanation.definitionFit: The furlong is an eighth of a mile, a unit of length used in horse racing.
